title: Study to evaluate the long-term safety and tolerability of nizubaglustat in people with rare lysosomal disorders who have previously participated in a nizubaglustat study and wish to continue treatment
official: An open-label, roll-over trial to evaluate the long-term safety and tolerability of nizubaglustat (AZ-3102) in participants with rare lysosomal disorders who have participated in previous nizubaglustat trials and wish to continue nizubaglustat treatment
summary: Main objective: To assess the long-term safety and  tolerability of continued daily administration of nizubaglustat.
conditions: GM1 gangliosidosis, GM2 gangliosidosis, Niemann-Pick disease type C, Gaucher disease type 3
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Previously participated in a trial of nizubaglustat and wish to continue in this OLE trial.
2. Participation is supported and deemed beneficial by the Principal Investigator.
3. Willing and able to be evaluated for protocol assessments.
4. The participant or their parent(s) and/or legal guardian(s) have read, understood, and signed  the ICF. Assent will also be sought for participants deemed not able to provide consent.
5. Females of childbearing potential, defined as postmenarchal and premenopausal female  capable of becoming pregnant, are eligible if they:  • Are sexually inactive and willing to stay sexually inactive during the trial (sexual  abstinence for the 14 days prior to the first dose of nizubaglustat and confirmation of  continued abstinence until 28 days after the last dose) OR • Using one of the following highly-effective contraceptives (i.e. <1% failure rate when used  consistently and correctly) for 14 days prior to the first dose of nizubaglustat and continuing  until 28 days after the last dose: intrauterine device; surgical sterilization of the partner  (vasectomy for a minimum of 6 months); combined  (estrogen- and progestogen-containing) hormonal contraception associated with inhibition  of ovulation (oral, intravaginal, or transdermal); progestogen-only hormonal contraception  associated with inhibition of ovulation (oral, injectable, or implantable, or intrauterine  hormone-releasing system).
6. Females of non-childbearing potential are eligible if they: • Have undergone one of the following sterilization operations at least 6 months prior to  receiving the first dose of nizubaglustat: hysteroscopic sterilization; bilateral  salpingectomy; hysterectomy; bilateral oophorectomy OR  • Are postmenopausal with at least 1 year of amenorrhea and follicle-stimulating hormone  (FSH) serum values consistent with postmenopausal status. At Screening, postmenopausal  women will have their FSH levels analyzed by the site’s local laboratory. FSH levels should  fall within the postmenopausal range OR • Are pre-menarchal at Screening and agree to stay sexually inactive during the trial and until  28 days after the last dose or are using one of the contraceptive methods listed in inclusion  criterion 5.
7. Non-vasectomized male participants must consent to use a spermicide-impregnated condom  or abstain from sexual activity until 90 days after the last dose of nizubaglustat; their female  partner is required to consent to comply with this inclusion criterion.
8. Vasectomized male participants who had the procedure at least 6 months before starting the  trial must consent to use a condom during sexual activity. Men vasectomized less than  6 months before starting the trial must adhere to the same restrictions as a non-vasectomized  male participants.
9. Male participants agree not to donate sperm from the start of treatment until 90 days after the  last dose of nizubaglustat. Female participants agree not to donate eggs from the start of  treatment until 90 days after the last dose (though this would not be permitted because of the  nature of the underlying disease).
Exclusion criteria:
1. A  positive serum pregnancy test (for women of childbearing potential).
2. Any medical event or condition that prevents participation in the trial based on the judgment  of the Principal Investigator (e.g., severe infection and severe cognitive impairment).
3. Use of any other treatment with a similar mode of action to nizubaglustat (GCS or NLGase inhibition), e.g., miglustat or venglustat
4. Participation in another interventional trial or non-interventional study or in an Early Access Program
